text: ILO Trends 2026: unemployment 4.9% (186 million). SOFI 2026: hunger fell for the 3rd year to 7.8%. Emissions Gap 2026 (UNEP, Oct 2026, "The Point of Return"): current policies → about 2.8°C; full NDCs → 2.6°C.

Latest: monthly PLFS (CWS) rate 4.9% in October 2026 (5.0% September); 30-35 million seasonal labourers migrate every year (7 Sep 2026).

Expansions: 2024 – ASHA, Anganwadi workers and helpers and families; Ayushman Vay Vandana card (Oct 2024) – Rs 5 lakh for all aged 70+ regardless of income. Odisha and Delhi joined in April 2025; West Bengal is the latest to join (MoU with NHA, 8 June 2026) – the 36th State/UT, so PM-JAY now runs in all States/UTs.
APPSC G1: a CRR hike causes fall in money circulation and low demand for goods and services (I and II); it does NOT raise purchasing power or the banks' lending capacity.
CRR applies to the whole NDTL; the I-CRR applied only to the incremental deposit base (not to "new borrowers") (APPSC G1 2024).

SLR: minimum share of NDTL a bank keeps with itself in liquid assets before lending – cash, gold and unencumbered approved/Government securities (G-secs, T-bills, SDLs); not priority-sector loans (APPSC G1 2023: I, II and III).

APPSC G1 2024 statements: CRR hike reduces credit creation (I ✗); I-CRR targeted incremental deposits, not borrowers (II ✗); tenor premium is an MCLR component (III ✓); MSF is an overnight rate equal to Bank Rate, not long-term or lower (IV ✗) → only III.
NSE chair: Girish Chandra Chaturvedi became chairman in Dec 2019 (term ended July 2024); now Srinivas Injeti, chairperson of the NSE Governing Board from 9 Sep 2025 (as of 2026).
Most moons: Saturn – 274 after 128 were confirmed (March 2025); 2026 additions by the Minor Planet Center (11 in March, 7 in April, 1 in June) → Saturn 293, Jupiter 115 (as of June 2026).

Odd ones: Humboldt is NOT warm (APPSC G1); Agulhas is NOT cold; Kuroshio is NOT cold; Canary is NOT warm and not in the Pacific; Benguela does not flow in the North Atlantic; Peruvian is the only Pacific current among Benguela, Brazil, South Equatorial.
Best fishing grounds form where warm and cold ocean currents meet (mixing brings nutrients and plankton), mainly between 40° and 60° – asked 4 times (APPSC G1 2002 twice, UPSC 2013 twice).
APPSC Group 1: Peru warm current + "Christ child" + 2014 Indian rainfall deficit = all three correct.

Units: decibel = sound level; light year = distance; 1 horsepower = 746 W; resistivity – ohm-metre; conductance – siemens, older mho; conductivity – S/m; e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; conventional current flows positive to negative.

Electrical energy = VIt; Joule's law of heating H = I²Rt; Kirchhoff's first (junction) law: current in = current out; Fleming's left-hand rule – middle finger = current, forefinger = field, thumb = force.
Magnetic meridian = vertical plane through a freely suspended magnet's axis; a current-carrying wire makes a magnetic field (deflects a compass – Oersted).
EM induction = current induced in a coil by relative motion of magnet and coil (changing flux) – Faraday.
Slip-ring induction motor: started with full external rotor resistance; adding rotor resistance raises starting torque and lowers starting current.
Series resistors: Rs = R1 + R2 + … – net resistance increases; the same current flows through all.
Ammeter measures current (in series); voltmeter – potential difference (parallel); galvanometer detects small current; rheostat varies resistance.
Transformer losses (heating): copper (I²R), hysteresis, eddy currents, flux leakage.
Fleming's left-hand rule = force on a current in a magnetic field (motor); right-hand rule = induced current (generator).
Induced current: maximum when the conductor moves perpendicular to the field; in a rotating coil it reverses every half revolution (AC).
Choke of a tube light = an inductor: starting voltage surge, then limits current.
Parallel resistors share the same potential difference (current divides); series resistors carry the same current. Household wiring is parallel.
Faraday's law: faster magnet motion → faster flux change → larger induced current.
Insulators are charged by static electricity (friction/rubbing – comb, glass rod); current electricity flows only through conductors.
SI units in electricity: charge – coulomb; current – ampere; potential difference – volt; resistance – ohm.
Gas laws: Boyle (PV const; V vs 1/p = straight line), Charles (V ∝ T), Avogadro, Gay-Lussac's combining volumes (simple volume ratios); Joule's law is about heating by current, not a gas law.
SI units: joule – energy/work; pascal (N/m²) – pressure; watt – power; newton – force; kelvin – temperature; ampere – current; candela – luminous intensity.
Transformer: the low-voltage winding carries more current → larger cross-section, fewer turns.
Heating coil: H = I²Rt = V²t/R – depends on voltage, current and time.
Parallel wires: currents in the same direction attract, opposite directions repel.
States of matter: solid, liquid, gas, plasma (4th), Bose–Einstein condensate (5th, latest; predicted by S.N. Bose & Einstein, made in 1995).
Step-down transformer: lowers voltage and raises current (power nearly constant); step-up – the reverse; works only on AC.
Ohm's law V = IR – voltage across a fixed resistor (e.g. nichrome) rises linearly with current.
Wire falling along East–West: cuts Earth's horizontal field, so current is induced West → East (Fleming's right-hand rule).
Resistance – unit ohm (Ω); volt = potential difference; ampere = current.
Dimensions: current [I], length [L], time [T], mass [M] – A·m/s² = [I L T⁻²].
Electromagnetism: a changing magnetic field induces current (Faraday); current produces a magnetic field (Oersted).
Resistance depends on length, area of cross-section, material (resistivity) and temperature – not on the current through it.
Fundamental (SI base) quantities: length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount, luminous intensity; weight is a force (derived); mass = amount of matter, same everywhere.
Galvanometer = detects the presence (and direction) of current; refractometer – refractive index; viscometer – viscosity.
Ohm's law: V = IR – potential difference ∝ current at constant temperature.
Chemical effect of current: current through a conducting liquid causes a chemical reaction (electrolysis, electroplating).
Gas laws: Boyle (PV const; V vs 1/p = straight line), Charles (V ∝ T), Avogadro, Gay-Lussac's combining volumes (simple volume ratios); Joule's law is about heating by current, not a gas law.
Electroplating: passing electric current through a metal-salt solution deposits a thin film (gold on jewellery, chromium on taps, zinc/tin on iron).
Short circuit: resistance ≈ 0 → current increases heavily; a fuse melts on heavy current.
Galvanometer: detects current and its direction; null detector in bridges; more sensitive, not more accurate, than an ammeter.

Instruments: hygrometer – humidity; ammeter – current; odometer – distance; anemometer – wind speed; tachometer – rotational speed (rpm); pyrometer – very high temperature; hydrometer – relative density of liquids; epidiascope – projects opaque objects and transparencies.
Ammeter (in series) measures current; voltmeter – potential difference.
SI base units: current – ampere; temperature – kelvin; luminous intensity – candela; mass – kg; length – m; time – s; amount – mole.

Crude-oil reserves: 672.07 million tonnes (as on 1.4.2025); earlier 671.4 MT (as on 1.4.2024) and 651.77 MT (MoSPI Energy Statistics 2024, as on 1.4.2023).
Step-up transformer raises voltage (and lowers current) for long-distance transmission; it does not raise power.
DG set starting current: motor starting current should not exceed about 200% (twice) of the DG set's full-load current (printed key).
